contributions.statement: For dependency upgrades, expect LLM repair to handle renames and import migrations but plan human review for paradigm-shift breaking changes, which were solved in only 65-70% of cases even by the best method.
contributions.evidence: §V-G Table VII; per-cell rates rest on 9-27 instances; all 38 Maven cases are JUnit 4->5 or Spring Boot 2.7->3.0 (contamination-prone), and import migration was 100% even for the no-evidence baseline.

contributions.statement: Do not paste raw upstream changelogs into an agent brief for a dependency upgrade; distill them into explicit old-to-new rules with affected call sites first.
contributions.evidence: Table V: raw upstream evidence cut pass rates 7-23 pp; audit grades weak (single temperature-0 runs, agents denied in-loop build/test). Table VI: on Opus, rules+locator without type guidance scored 61.1%, below the 71.6% no-evidence baseline, so partial distillation can also hurt.

reason: Java/Maven-relevant boundary on which migration types LLMs still miss is usable for routing review; the raw-changelog warning is a hypothesis because agents were handicapped and runs are single.
